body.statement:
For every \(m\in\mathcal M_3\), there is an open neighborhood of \((0,0)\) in \(\mathbb R^2\) such that, for every \((t_0,u_0)\) in that neighborhood, \(A_m(t_0,u_0)\) is invertible and the tuple \(m'_{t_0,u_0}=(a(m),b'_{m,t_0,u_0},c'_{m,t_0,u_0},d(m),
u'_{m,t_0,u_0})\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_3\). More explicitly, \(K'_{m,t_0,u_0}=A_m(t_0,u_0)K_m= egin{pmatrix}1&-a(m)&0\-b'_{m,t_0,u_0}&1&-c'_{m,t_0,u_0}\0&-d(m)&1\end{pmatrix}\), \(K'_{m,t_0,u_0}X=A_m(t_0,u_0)K_mX=A_m(t_0,u_0)\varepsilon=\varepsilon'_{m,t_0,u_0}\), and hence \(m'_{t_0,u_0}\) induces exactly \(P_m\). On this neighborhood, \(b'_{m,t_0,u_0}c'_{m,t_0,u_0}
eq0\), \(1-a(m)b'_{m,t_0,u_0}-c'_{m,t_0,u_0}d(m)=(1+a(m)t_0+d(m)u_0)\Delta(m)
eq0\), \(E_m[\varepsilon'_i]=0\), and \(E_m[|\varepsilon'_i|^3]<\infty\) for every \(i\in I\). The middle coordinate obeys \[\|\varepsilon'_2-\varepsilon_2\|_{L^3(m)}\le |t_0|\|\varepsilon_1\|_{L^3(m)}+|a(m)t_0+d(m)u_0|\|\varepsilon_2\|_{L^3(m)}+|u_0|\|\varepsilon_3\|_{L^3(m)}\longrightarrow0.\] Thus the neighborhood can be chosen so that its middle marginal is non-Gaussian, since otherwise Gaussian transformed middle marginals along a sequence converging to the origin would converge weakly to the non-Gaussian law of \(\varepsilon_2\); the endpoint marginals are unchanged and non-Gaussian. Moreover, \(\varepsilon'_1=\varepsilon_1\) and \(\varepsilon'_3=\varepsilon_3\), so \(\varepsilon'_1\perp\!\!\!\perp\varepsilon'_3\) and the path connected-set Markov restriction is preserved. Independence genericity is preserved because any nonzero independent pair of linear forms in \(\varepsilon'\), pulled back by \(A_m(t_0,u_0)^	op\), must lie on the two opposite endpoint axes under the genericity of \(m\), while \(A_m(t_0,u_0)^{-	op}(1,0,0)^	op=(1,0,0)^	op\) and \(A_m(t_0,u_0)^{-	op}(0,0,1)^	op=(0,0,1)^	op\). The induced map \((t_0,u_0)\mapsto(b'_{m,t_0,u_0},c'_{m,t_0,u_0})\) has derivative determinant \(\Delta(m)
eq0\) at the origin. Hence the compatible full-law fiber in \((b,c)\) contains a two-dimensional neighborhood while the outer projection is a singleton whenever \(D(P_m)
eq0\).
body.justification: The explicit pushforward law and two-sided genericity calculation certify that the same-law shear stays inside the maintained non-Gaussian path model, separating recoverable outer mechanisms from a legal central sensitivity fiber.
body.gap: Lacerda and coauthors describe cyclic LiNG equivalence under mutually independent errors, while the Gaussian group theorem of Draisma, Kuhnt, and Zwiernik does not establish legality under this non-Gaussian path model.
body.consumer: A prospective BayCausal or Women's Interagency HIV Study extension can report the outer coefficients and display \((b,c)\) as a same-law sensitivity surface.
